question: What is known to be ‘ekaharya’, where one dancer takes on many roles in a single performance?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharatanatyam**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Bharatnatyam dance is a dance form of Tamil Nadu which is also known to be as ekaharya, where one dancer takes on several roles in a single performance.
 
• It is also known as Dasiattam.
 
• The Brihadeeswara Temple at Thanjavur has been a centre for Bharatanatyam since 1000 CE.
 
• In its usual form, the dance is generally divided into seven main parts – Alarippu, Jatiswaran, Shabda, Varna, Pada, Thillana and Sloka.
 
• Mrinalini Sarabhai, Shobhana, Yamini Krishnamurthy, Padma Subrahmanyam, and Chithra Vishveshwaran 
 
 
• ​are some of the famous contemporaries of the Bharatnatyam Dance form.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Kathak:​

 
 
• ​This dance originated in North India.
 
• It was largely a temple or village performance wherein the dancers narrated stories from ancient scriptures.
 
 
 
• Kuchipudi:
 
 
• Kuchipudi is the name of a village in the Krishna district of Andhra Pradesh which has a long custom of dance-drama.
 
 
 
• Kathakali:
 
 
• Kathakali is a blend of dance, music, and acting and dramatizes stories, which are mostly adapted from Indian epics
 
• Different facial colors indicate different mental stages & characters, e.g. green – nobility, black – wicked, red patches – combining royalty & evil.
 
 

ea:T
